candidates.description: Simple and flexible tool for managing secrets
evidence: README supports YAML/JSON/ENV/INI/BINARY and age/KMS backends under MPL-2.0.
CLI source offers encryption/decryption and exec-env; exec-env deliberately injects decrypted values into a child environment.

candidates.next: Keep native client sign-in local; consider SOPS only for explicitly owned service configuration with recipients/recovery owners defined. Do not inject broker secrets into research workers.

candidates.description: A simple, modern and secure encryption tool (and Go library) with small explicit keys, no config options, and UNIX-style composability.
candidates.role: Portable file encryption and recovery-key envelope
evidence: README and CLI source provide explicit recipient and identity-file encryption/decryption commands.
Selected tests exercise recipient-file parsing; the source license is BSD-3-Clause.
Encryption does not supply off-host storage, independent key custody, or restore/cutover proof.
candidates.next: Use only when it improves a chosen recovery design; existing Restic encryption already covers its repositories, so avoid redundant envelopes by default.

candidates.description: OpenSSF Scorecard - Security health metrics for Open Source
evidence: Upstream check docs describe limitations, including incomplete branch-protection observations without administrative access.
License check delegates to detected source/license evidence; API classification can be unknown even when a license file exists.
Scores are heuristic security-practice signals, not quality, correctness, trading performance, or trustworthy dependency proof.
candidates.next: Optionally inspect selected check findings for adopted dependencies; retain exact version, date, permissions and unknown checks. No score was fetched or invented.

candidates.next: Start from existing pinned actions, least permissions and native logs. Consider only after endpoint allowlist and external observation policy are selected.

candidates.description: A framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks.
evidence: run.py treats files modified by a hook as failure even if the hook command returns zero.
Selected tests include failing hooks and a hook that modifies files while returning zero.
A hook framework can execute selected third-party code and create tool environments; it is not a sandbox or runtime evidence.
candidates.next: Reuse current validation commands first. If adopted, pin selected hook revisions and preserve native Codex/Claude lifecycle hooks; do not install broad hook packs.

governance.current_state: 453 indexed identities, 152 cards representing 147 repositories, and a separate six-candidate portability supplement whose five new identities raise the actual reviewed-reference union to 458.
governance.gap: validate_catalogs.py validates the four card files, their core coverage and star audit, but not the grand Markdown table or supplemental identity union.
governance.proposed_index: Authoritative typed decision-index.json generated from public-star coverage, star reviews, four catalog cards, adopted component records, legacy candidates and explicitly registered research supplements.
rules: Use canonical owner/repository identities with verified aliases; preserve source paths and exact JSON pointers.
Keep discovery-only links outside reviewed/adopted counts unless explicitly registered with their true depth and disposition.
Compute counts and references; reject omitted source membership, alias cycles, duplicate canonical records, unsafe pointers and stale counts.
Preserve historical receipts and source-review limitations; source review never implies native execution.
Future supplement ingestion must name an explicit repository-entry collection; do not recursively treat every URL in prose as a selected repository.

retained_failures: Native gh rejects --slurp with --jq; corrected to paginated JSON lines before public filtering.
hkdobrev/awesome-fintech returned 404; replaced with the verified jplock company directory, without inferring why the first endpoint failed.
GitHub README JSON content was absent/truncated for two large lists; repeated with exact pinned raw content and byte-size checks.
An overlarge extracted-link capture exceeded output allowance; repeated with compact identity strings and aggregate categories.
limits: 7028 extracted GitHub owner/repository links are not 7028 metadata checks or source reviews. Only ten new candidate repositories received selected-file review.
Six of the ten candidates came from capability-led primary-source follow-up rather than a directly extracted GitHub link; website/relative example links were not exhaustively mapped.
The list parser covers complete pinned root README files, not every nested index, issue, PR, translation, website or externally linked project.
The 6939 other linked identities remain discovery-only and unassessed. Their archived flags, licenses and canonical redirects were not fetched.
No installation, service/model call, provider change, broker call, security score, profitability claim, paid account or recurring automation was performed.
No universal saturation or definitive-best ranking is claimed. Subsequent source discovery can still uncover missing capabilities.
